- When sentiment is negative and price is trending upward, model tends to overestimate near-term peaks; reduce forecast peak heights by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a 3–5 day lag correction downward.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model underestimates downward momentum; add 2–4% bias upward to forecast.
- Mean reversion is stronger in 10–14 day horizons; if model forecasts >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 3–7%.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates late-period rallies; increase final 5–7 days by 2–5% if sentiment turns positive.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model tends to overforecast; apply 1–3% downward adjustment to all forecasts.
